note.question: When should competing two-sided platforms impose high or low provider quality standards, and when do private platform incentives diverge from a regulator's preferred quality regime?
note.overview: The model has two competing platforms making strategic quality-standard and price choices. The paper analyzes equilibrium outcomes but does not attach a separate Nash/SPNE refinement name, so none is invented here.

models.method: The paper identifies concrete situations wherein the platforms diverge in the enforcement of service standards.

sources.quote: The prices imposed by the platforms result in one of the following supply-demand matching scenarios: CcMp, where they compete for consumers but monopolize the enrollment of providers; McCp, where they monop­ olize the enrollment of consumers but compete for providers; McMp, where they monopolize the enroll­ ment of providers and consumers; or CcCp, where they compete for providers and consumers.

sources.section: 4.1. Pricing Strategies in a Given Profile of Service Standards
sources.quote: Specifically, the two platforms manage scenario CcMp when λ is small (i.e., the area delimited by λHH,a1 and λHH,c1 in Figure 2(a)), in which case the abundance of providers entices the platforms to serve all consumers but keep off a proportion of providers, but they manage scenario McCp when λ is large (i.e., the area delimited by λHH,c2 and λHH,b1 in Figure 2(a)), in which case the large consumer size leads the plat­ forms to monopolize the enrollment of consumers but compete to enroll all providers.
